still: A photograph taken by a small unattended lens fixed in the sloped ceiling above a rented attic room, looking straight down at a single bed under the rafters at night. Brandon lies on his back with the duvet to his chest, his face lit pale blue-white from below by the phone held above him, the phone's face turned away from the lens. The rest of the attic is almost black, with grainy night-mode noise, washed-out compressed colour, and a bare floorboard gap at the edge of the frame. The angle is high, wide and flat, and Brandon is small in the frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon, small in the wide high view, lies still in bed with the phone held above his face, then taps once with his thumb and lets the hand drop to the duvet. Later he gives a slow blink and his brows lift slightly. The glow on his face dims a little. Night-mode grain shimmers in the dark corners of the rafters. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Soft thumb tap on glass, duvet rustle, a faint creak of rafters, a distant fridge hum from downstairs. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a webcam-style lens fixed on a bookshelf at the end of the attic, looking along the room at a single bed under a sloped ceiling in flat morning daylight. A skylight blows out to near white and the rest of the room is washed out and slightly soft. Brandon sits bolt upright in the bed, the duvet bunched at his waist, both palms flat on his own cheeks, eyes wide, brows high and mouth open in an astonished O. A mug and a crumpled hoodie sit on the floorboards by the bed. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon sits bolt upright and pats his cheeks with both palms, three quick pats, eyes wide and brows high. Later his hands drop to his lap, he looks down at himself and his mouth widens into a disbelieving grin. Dust drifts in the shaft of light from the skylight. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Quick soft palm slaps on skin, duvet fabric shifting, a pigeon walking on the skylight glass, floorboard creak. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed high in the corner of a cramped attic, looking down diagonally at a pine desk under a bare bulb. Brandon sits at the desk with a printed sheaf of paper flat in front of him, one finger under a line of text that is too small to read, his mouth slightly open and brows raised in wonder. A desk lamp with a cracked plastic shade, a cold mug and a wire pen pot crowd the desk. The light is a single warm bulb plus a grey window, with heavy grain and washed-out colour. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon slides his finger slowly along the line of the printed paper, lips parting wider as he reads. Later he looks up at the sloped ceiling with his brows high, then back down and resumes under the next line. The bare bulb flickers once and steadies. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Paper rasp under a fingertip, a slow mouth-breath, the buzz of the bare bulb, a distant bus passing outside. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed high above a narrow bathroom door, looking down into a small bathroom with chipped white tiles and one fluorescent tube overhead giving flat green-white light. Brandon stands at the sink facing the mirror, a toothbrush in his mouth, his jaw set, brows pulled low and eyes locked on his own reflection with fighter-like intent. Limescale rings the tap and a damp towel hangs on a radiator. The image is washed out and compressed, and Brandon is small in the frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon brushes in firm, even strokes, jaw set and eyes unblinking on the mirror. Later he leans in a fraction, narrows his eyelids and gives a single sharp nod to himself. The fluorescent tube hums and flickers once. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Rhythmic bristle scrub, a tap dripping slowly, the electrical buzz of the tube, a pipe knocking in the wall. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed in the ceiling corner of the attic, looking down at a single bed in grey daylight from a small window. Brandon kneels on the mattress tucking the duvet edge tight under the mattress with both hands, brows drawn together, tongue pressed in one cheek, eyes on the corner. The bed is flat and square, the floorboards are swept and the clothes are folded in a pile on a crate. The picture is soft, washed out and a little noisy. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon tucks the duvet under the mattress with both hands along one side, smoothing it flat with a sweep of his palm. Later he sits back on his heels, looks over the finished bed and gives a small satisfied nod. A dust mote drifts through the window light. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Cotton fabric dragging over a mattress, palm smoothing, a floorboard creak, soft wind at the window. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed high on a bathroom wall, looking down at a cramped space under a basin where a narrow cupboard door stands open. Brandon lies on his side on a dry lino floor with head and shoulders under the sink, a spanner in one hand, the other hand on a chrome isolation valve, a small torch clamped in his teeth lighting the pipes. His brows are lifted and his eyes crinkled with delight. The floor is dry and the colours are washed out. A single overhead strip light lights the room. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon turns the chrome valve a quarter turn with the spanner, then stops and looks at the pipe. Later he lifts one thumb in the air and his eyes crinkle. The overhead strip light hums. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Metal on metal, a faint tick of pipework, torch beam clicking, a quiet pleased exhale through the nose. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed near the ceiling at the foot of an attic bed, looking along it at night in dim night-mode grain. Brandon sleeps on his back under a neat duvet, mouth slightly open, brows smooth, eyelids closed. A strip of dental floss lies coiled on a wooden crate beside the bed next to a glass of water. A bar of streetlight orange comes through a small window and lies across the floorboards. The rest is deep shadow, washed out and compressed. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon sleeps without stirring, the duvet rising and falling with his breathing. Later he turns his head a few degrees on the pillow and his mouth closes. The streetlight bar flickers once as something passes outside. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Slow steady breathing, a faint fabric rustle, a car passing far below, a distant fox cry. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed above the doorway of a small shop, looking down and across a narrow pavement and a town high street in flat grey daylight. Brandon walks along the pavement past parked cars and a bin, one hand holding a phone at hip height, its screen turned away from the lens, his gaze straight ahead. Wet paving, a lamp post and brick terraces give the scene washed-out colour and slight lens distortion at the edges. He is small in the frame. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon walks across the frame from right to left at an even pace, thumb tapping the phone at his hip once without his eyes dropping from the road ahead. Later he steps past a lamp post and exits at the edge of the frame. A plastic bag stirs on the kerb. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Steady footsteps on damp paving, a car passing on the road, a pigeon wing flap, a faint thumb tap on glass. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed high in the corner of a small kitchen, looking diagonally down at a laminate table under one fluorescent ring light. Brandon sits alone at the table, head bowed over a white plate of steamed broccoli, carrots and boiled potatoes, hands pressed together in front of his chin, eyelids closed and brows slightly drawn. A single cup, a salt pot and a wipe-clean tablecloth fill the surface. The image is washed out and slightly blurry from compression. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon holds his bowed head and pressed hands very still over the plate. Later he opens his eyes, unclasps his hands and picks up a fork. The fluorescent ring light buzzes and dims faintly. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Fork tines clinking on china, a fridge motor humming, a tap dripping, a chair leg shifting on lino. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed at the top of a lamp post, looking down steeply at a suburban street in flat overcast daylight. Brandon jogs along the pavement, small and foreshortened from above, in a loose grey tracksuit and with an easy, upright stride, his face turned forward and calm. In the road beside him a white ambulance with a blank side panel rolls slowly past, and Sophie sits in the passenger window looking out at him with her brows drawn together and her mouth closed. Wet tarmac, a postbox and parked cars give washed-out, compressed colour. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon jogs steadily along the pavement from the left of the frame while the ambulance rolls slowly forward beside him on the right. Sophie's head turns to follow him through the window. Later Brandon jogs out of frame and the ambulance crawls on, its brake lights glowing. A leaf spins along the gutter. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Rhythmic running footfalls, a low diesel engine idle, tyres on wet tarmac, a distant dog bark. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a doorbell-style lens fixed beside a glass door at a small gym entrance, looking out toward a rain-damp car park in wide, slightly bent perspective. Brandon stands on the step outside the front door with his head tipped down at a phone in his hand, its screen turned away, then his head is half-turned over his shoulder as if sensing something behind him, brows pinched and eyes wide. The light is overcast grey with a sodium glow in the glass behind. The colour is washed out with a hint of fisheye distortion. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon stands on the step looking down at the phone in his hand. Then he turns his head slowly over his shoulder toward the car park behind him, brows pinching. Later he blinks and shifts his weight to the other foot. A strip of rain drips from the door canopy. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Rain dripping from a canopy, a car door thunk far away, the hum of a fluorescent sign, shoe soles on a wet step. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed high in the corner of a plain, under-lit gym room, looking down across rubber flooring, a bench and a rack of dumbbells under one flickering strip light. Brandon on the left of the frame faces right, talking with his eyebrows high and his mouth wide, one hand gesturing. Gary on the right of the frame stands stiff in a stiff, brand-new grey gym t-shirt and black shorts with a blank cardboard price tag still dangling from the hem, looking at him with a fixed, blank face. The image is soft, washed out and slightly noisy. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon, on the left, talks and gestures with his hand while Gary, on the right, stands still with his arms at his sides. Later Gary glances once toward the door and back, and Brandon keeps talking. The strip light flickers. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. A flickering tube buzz, rubber soles squeaking, a distant treadmill belt, muffled dumbbell clunks, a rustle of stiff new fabric. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed in the corner of the ceiling of a gym changing area, looking down at a low wooden bench against tiled walls under a flat fluorescent panel. Brandon on the left of the frame sits forward with his elbows on his knees, mouth open mid-flow and brows raised, one hand open in the air. Gary on the right of the frame stands holding a folded white towel, his eyelids half-lowered and his mouth flat, gazing at nothing. Colours are washed out and slightly green, with soft grain. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Brandon, on the left, rocks and gestures with one open hand, talking without pause. Gary, on the right, stays rigid, the towel hanging from both hands. Later Gary's eyes slide to Brandon and back to the wall. The fluorescent panel buzzes. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Fluorescent panel buzz, a distant shower drip, sneakers squeaking, a locker door clanging down the corridor. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.

still: A photograph from a lens fixed high on a gym wall, looking down at a juice-bar counter and a stool area under a bare tube light, in washed-out colour and grain. Gary on the right of the frame holds out a plastic shaker bottle of thick beige liquid toward Brandon on the left. Brandon beams, his brows high, his eyes crinkled and his mouth wide open, reaching with both hands. Gary's face is blank and motionless, and his eyes stay locked on Brandon. A towel is slung across the counter. Thanks.
motion: The camera does not move. Gary, on the right, extends the shaker bottle and Brandon, on the left, takes it with both hands, beaming. Later Brandon looks down at the bottle while Gary's gaze stays fixed on Brandon's face with a blank, unblinking stare. The tube light flickers faintly. Shot at 24fps with a 180-degree shutter, so fast movement smears. The camera does not move. Plastic bottle rattle, a tube light buzz, rubber soles on the floor, a distant machine whirr. No dialogue, no music. Thanks.
